title: Praise on Thee, in Zion's Gates
description: Praise on Thee, in Zion's Gates in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 882 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Thou crownest the year with goodness."”, where the book credits them to the Ev. Magazine.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise on thee, in Zi-on's gates, Dail-y, O Je-ho-vah! waits; Un-to thee, O God! be-long Grate-ful words and ho-ly song.

lines: Praise on thee, in Zion's gates,
Thou the hope and refuge art
Thou dost visit earth, and rain
From the copious founts on high,
From the rivers of the sky.
Thus the clouds thy power confess,
And the voice of song and mirth
Rises from the tribes of earth.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
